messages.content:
What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Redacted]
Sex: Female
Age: 29 Years
Hospital: Orašje County Hospital (Bosnia and Herzegovina)
Admission Date: [Redacted]
Discharge Date: [Redacted]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
A 29-year-old female was admitted to the Department of Surgery with a history of recurrent colicky right upper quadrant abdominal pain. The patient was diagnosed as having multiple gallstones within the gallbladder on abdominal ultrasonography. Routine hematological and biochemical test results were normal. The patient underwent elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy, and there were no complications during the procedure, or postoperatively. The patient was discharged on the third postoperative day. 

Pathology Report:
Histologically, microscopic slides from the gallbladder body showed that almost the entire cylindrical epithelium of the mucosa was missing. There was a moderate mixed inflammatory cell infiltrate in the submucosa, and the muscular layer was slightly hypertrophic, which is consistent with chronic cholecystitis. The most unusual feature of the slide from the body of the gallbladder was the presence of large dilated vessels within the muscular layer extending into the submucosa and mucosa. The appearance of angiodysplasia of the gallbladder and its endothelial lining was confirmed immunohistochemically using CD34, CD31, and podoplanin (D2-40) monoclonal antibodies. 

Follow-up:
The patient remained healthy at 6-year follow-up. 

Summary:
The patient, a 29-year-old woman, underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy for multiple gallstones within the gallbladder. The histopathological findings revealed chronic cholecystitis with the unusual feature of angiodysplasia of the gallbladder. There were no complications during the procedure, and the patient was discharged on the third postoperative day. The patient remained healthy at the 6-year follow-up.

text:
The principal diagnosis is most likely **K80.1, Calculus of gallbladder with other cholecystitis**.

The admission was for recurrent right upper quadrant pain caused by gallstones, and the surgery treated them. The histopathology report describes chronic cholecystitis, and ICD-10-AM classifies chronic cholecystitis with gallstones under K80.1. Because the discharge diagnosis section is withheld, this depends on the treating clinicians documenting chronic cholecystitis as a final diagnosis. Coders usually need that confirmation before assigning a code based on pathology findings.

If chronic cholecystitis were not confirmed as a diagnosis, the code would be **K80.2, Calculus of gallbladder without cholecystitis**.

The gallbladder angiodysplasia is a secondary diagnosis and does not change the principal code.
